question: Who works the most hours per year?
stat_label: Average annual hours worked per worker
source_name: Penn World Table 11 via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Indonesia leads on long informal and farm hours. Greece still beats Germany because part-time work is rare there and common in Germany.
headline: Grindset Nations

question: Who drinks the most alcohol per person?
stat_label: Total alcohol per capita (age 15+), litres of pure alcohol
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: Romania leads because WHO counts home-distilled fruit brandy, not just shop bottles. Uganda passes Italy once home brew is included. Note: recorded plus unrecorded alcohol, adults 15+, 2020.
headline: Bottoms Up

question: Which country has the highest adult obesity rate?
stat_label: Adults (18+) with obesity, BMI ≥ 30 (crude estimate)
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory (via Our World in Data)
fun_fact: Egypt edges the US after a fast shift to cheap refined staples and less daily activity. France's rate stays far lower.
headline: Heavyweights

question: Where are people happiest with their lives?
stat_label: Life satisfaction (Cantril ladder, 0–10)
source_name: World Happiness Report / Wellbeing Research Centre via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Costa Rica and Mexico outscore the richer US and UK. These scores track social support and health more than income.
headline: Happy Places

question: Which country has the highest homicide rate?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people
source_name: UNODC via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: The US rate is about twice India's, largely because civilian gun ownership is far higher and most US homicides are shootings. Note: latest years differ by country.
headline: Homicide Rates

question: Where are women the biggest share of STEM graduates?
stat_label: Female share of tertiary STEM graduates
source_name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: Women are a majority of STEM graduates in Algeria, and under 30% in Germany.
headline: Lab Coats

question: Who lives the longest?
stat_label: Life expectancy at birth
source_name: World Bank, World Development Indicators (UN Population Division)
fun_fact: Babies in Chile and Costa Rica can expect about two more years than babies in the US. The US shortfall clusters in guns, drugs, obesity and uneven care.
headline: Long Livers

question: Where do women have the most children?
stat_label: Total fertility rate (births per woman)
source_name: World Bank, World Development Indicators (UN Population Division)
fun_fact: Israel's rate stays high because religious Jewish families have many children. Iran fell to US and French levels after a national family-planning program from 1989.
headline: Fertility Rate

question: Which parliament has the most women?
stat_label: Seats held by women in national parliament
source_name: Inter-Parliamentary Union via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: Rwanda has led for years: its 2003 constitution reserves at least 30% of seats for women, and women then won far more than that quota.
headline: Madam Speaker

question: Which drivers are most likely to be in a fatal crash per mile driven?
stat_label: US passenger-vehicle driver fatal crash involvements per 100 million miles
source_name: IIHS Fatality Facts: Males and females (FARS + NHTS)
fun_fact: Teen drivers top this list per mile because inexperience meets low mileage. Over 70, women's rate exceeds men's, reversing the all-ages pattern. Note: fatal involvements per 100 million miles, 2022.
headline: Fatal Crash Rates

question: Where is the female homicide rate highest?
stat_label: Intentional homicide victims, female
source_name: UNODC via World Bank, World Development Indicators (VC.IHR.PSRC.FE.P5)
fun_fact: The US female rate tops India's. Women killed in the US usually die by gunshot, often a partner. Note: UNODC via World Bank, 2022.
headline: Female Homicide

question: Where is the homicide rate highest, by sex?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 of that sex (male or female population)
source_name: UNODC via World Bank, World Development Indicators (VC.IHR.PSRC.MA.P5 / VC.IHR.PSRC.FE.P5)
fun_fact: US women are killed at a higher rate than men in Germany. In the US that is mostly gun homicide; male homicide in Germany is rare. Note: per 100,000 of that sex, 2022.
headline: Homicide by Sex

question: Where are women most likely to be in the workforce?
stat_label: Female labor force participation rate (% of women 15+, ILO modeled estimate)
source_name: ILO modeled estimates via World Bank, World Development Indicators (SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS)
fun_fact: Gulf reforms pulled women into jobs: the UAE now nearly matches the US, and Saudi women out-participate Indian women. Italy stays lower than the UAE.
headline: Working Women

question: Which country has the highest suicide rate?
stat_label: Age-standardized suicide rate, both sexes
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator MH_12 (Global Health Estimates)
fun_fact: South Korea leads because suicide is far more common among older adults in poverty. Sweden, despite the gloomy reputation, is lowest here. Note: WHO modelled, age-standardized, 2023.
headline: Suicide Rates

question: Whose lifestyle emits the most CO₂ per person?
stat_label: Consumption-based CO₂ emissions per person (emissions embedded in what a country consumes, incl. imports, minus exports)
source_name: Global Carbon Budget (Global Carbon Project) via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Singapore's footprint is so high because a rich city imports nearly everything it uses. Switzerland looks green on smokestacks but buys the emissions in its imports. Note: consumption-based CO2, 2023.
headline: Carbon Shoppers

question: Who emits the most CO₂ per person?
stat_label: Territorial fossil CO₂ emissions per person (fossil fuels and industry, excl. land use)
source_name: Global Carbon Budget (Global Carbon Project) via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Saudi Arabia leads on cheap oil, air conditioning and desalination. Australia slightly tops the US on coal-heavy power. An Indian emits about half what a Briton does. Note: territorial fossil CO2, not imports.
headline: Smokestacks

question: Where are 19-year-old women tallest?
stat_label: Mean height of 19-year-old girls
source_name: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC), Lancet 2020;396:1511-24
fun_fact: Chinese 19-year-old women are now as tall as American ones, after better childhood diets since the 1980s. US heights barely rose. Note: the top three overlap within uncertainty, so treat them as a near-tie.
headline: Tall Girls

question: Where are 19-year-old men tallest?
stat_label: Mean height of 19-year-old boys
source_name: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC), Lancet 2020;396:1511-24
fun_fact: China's 19-year-old men gained more height since 1985 than any other country, on better childhood nutrition, and are now close to Americans.
headline: Tall Guys

question: In Texas, who is most likely to be convicted of a crime?
stat_label: Criminal conviction rate (all crimes), Texas, 2013–2022 average
source_name: Cato Institute, Policy Analysis No. 977 (Nowrasteh, 2024), using Texas DPS data
fun_fact: Native-born Texans were convicted at about twice the rate of undocumented immigrants. Note: not adjusted for age or sex. Cato says non-homicide figures are less reliable because status is checked less often for minor crimes.
headline: Texas Convictions

question: In England & Wales, which citizens were most likely to be convicted?
stat_label: Approximate convictions per 10,000 residents aged 16+, by citizenship (non-citizens only; naturalised Britons count as UK)
source_name: Migration Observatory (Univ. of Oxford) analysis of MoJ conviction data and 2021 Census
fun_fact: British citizens had a higher conviction rate than the South Asian and Chinese nationals here. Note: naturalised people count as UK. This is citizenship, not ethnicity. Undercounted populations can inflate some rates.
headline: In the Dock

question: Which pupils score highest at GCSE in England?
stat_label: Average Attainment 8 score (out of 90), state-funded schools, England
source_name: Department for Education via GOV.UK Ethnicity facts and figures
fun_fact: Chinese and Indian pupils score highest. Within every ethnic group, pupils on free school meals score lower. Note: Attainment 8, state-funded schools, England, 2022/23.
headline: Top of the Class

question: Where are child sexual-abuse sentences longest?
stat_label: Average prison sentence for sexual abuse of a child under 12 (months)
source_name: WODC report 3130 (van Koppen, Wijkman & de Wilde, VU Amsterdam, 2021), Table 36
fun_fact: Ireland's sentences are so long because the maximum is life; Switzerland's maximum was 10 years. Note: foreign samples are only 4 to 17 rulings, and the authors say to be cautious.
headline: Child Abuse Sentences

question: Which group voted most for Trump in 2024?
stat_label: Share voting for Trump, 2024 presidential election (national exit poll)
source_name: CNN national exit poll (Edison Research for the National Election Pool), final weighting
fun_fact: Latino men backed Trump slightly more than White women did. Note: exit poll of about 23,000 voters. Subgroup margins are several points, and the Asian cells rest on a few hundred interviews.
headline: Trump Voters

question: Which American men most agree a woman should tend the home?
stat_label: % of men who agree women should tend home while men work
source_name: NORC General Social Survey 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024 (own tabulation, weight WTSSNRPS / WTSSNRPS_AS)
fun_fact: Hispanic and Black men were the most likely to say a woman should tend the home. Note: only the gaps versus White men are statistically clear. The Asian sample is about 295 men. Pooled GSS 2016-2024, weighted.
headline: Kitchen Debate

question: Who approves most of the switch from communism to a market economy?
stat_label: % approving the change to a market economy since 1989/1991, by country and age
source_name: Pew Research Center, Spring 2019 Global Attitudes Survey (European Public Opinion Three Decades After the Fall of Communism, p.23)
fun_fact: Young Bulgarians approve most. Older Russians, who lived through the 1990s crash, mostly disapprove. Czechs aged 60+, who lived under communism, still approve more than young Russians.
headline: Market Transition

question: Whose young men have the highest testosterone?
stat_label: Mean morning salivary testosterone, men 15–29
source_name: Ellison et al. 2002, Human Reproduction 17(12):3251-3 (Table I)
fun_fact: The gap tracks diet and workload. Well-fed Massachusetts men tested highest; the Ache, Tamang and Lese men faced harder work and thinner diets. Note: 15-24 men per community, not whole countries.
headline: Testosterone

question: Which American men most oppose special efforts to hire and promote women?
stat_label: % of men who oppose special efforts to hire/promote women
source_name: NORC General Social Survey 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024 (own tabulation; weights WTSSNRPS, WTSSNRPS_AS for 2022/24)
fun_fact: White men were the most opposed to special efforts to hire women, the reverse of who says a woman should tend the home. Note: the Asian sample is small, and answers also reflect views of affirmative action. Pooled GSS 2016-2024.
headline: Hiring Hang-ups

question: Which American men most oppose preferential hiring of women?
stat_label: % of men who oppose preferential hiring of women
source_name: NORC General Social Survey 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024 (own tabulation; weights WTSSNRPS, WTSSNRPS_AS for 2022/24)
fun_fact: Most men opposed preferential hiring of women. Black men were the exception, the only group under half. Note: Asian and Hispanic men are statistically tied, and the Asian sample is small. Pooled GSS 2016-2024.
headline: Preferential Hiring

question: Homicide rate: world cities. Which is highest?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 residents, 2024
source_name: Consejo Ciudadano para la Seguridad Pública y la Justicia Penal (CCSPJP, Mexico), "Ranking 2024 de las 50 ciudades más violentas del mundo"
fun_fact: Memphis nearly matches Johannesburg: guns and concentrated poverty. Note: an NGO list of 50 cities. It mixes metro areas with city limits, and its US counts run above FBI figures.
headline: City Homicide

question: Homicide rate: US vs the world. Which city is highest?
stat_label: Homicides per 100,000 residents, 2024 (official city/police figures; sources differ by country)
source_name: FBI Crime Data Explorer (Memphis PD, Chicago PD, 2024); SESNSP via Observatorio Interactivo de Incidencia Delictiva (Mexico City); SSP-SP (São Paulo city); ONS year ending Dec 2024 (Greater London)
fun_fact: São Paulo's murder rate is a fraction of Chicago's, and Mexico City is lower than Chicago too. Note: official figures from different agencies. Chicago's own count is higher, but the order holds.
headline: City Homicide, Mixed

question: Homicide rate: US cities (FBI). Which is highest?
stat_label: Murder and non-negligent manslaughter per 100,000 residents, 2024 (city police agency)
source_name: FBI Crime Data Explorer, Summary (SRS/NIBRS) agency data, 2024: murder & non-negligent manslaughter
fun_fact: Chicago's reputation outruns its rate: Memphis, Kansas City and Washington are all higher. Note: FBI murders by city police agency. New Orleans and Jackson, MS, did not report 2024, so they are unranked.
headline: US City Homicide

question: Who most approves of the switch from communism to a market economy?
stat_label: % who approve of the change to a market economy (Pew Spring 2019, Q16)
source_name: Pew Research Center, "European Public Opinion Three Decades After the Fall of Communism" (Oct 15, 2019), Spring 2019 Global Attitudes Survey
fun_fact: Slovakia's young adults approve far more than their parents. Young Russians are about as pro-market as older Slovaks. Note: age-group margins are about 5-8 points, so those two are tied.
headline: Capitalist Converts

question: Which group of Americans has the most positive view of socialism?
stat_label: % with a very or somewhat positive impression of "socialism" (Pew, Aug 1–14 2022)
source_name: Pew Research Center, "Modest Declines in Positive Views of 'Socialism' and 'Capitalism' in U.S." (Sep 19, 2022), survey of 7,647 adults (ATP Wave 113)
fun_fact: Black and Asian Americans view the word socialism more positively than adults under 30. Among under-30s it edges capitalism. Note: the groups overlap, and those three figures sit inside each other's margins.
headline: Views of Socialism

question: Who eats the most rice per person?
stat_label: Rice available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Bangladesh and the Philippines eat rice at almost every meal. China's average is lower because the north lives on wheat, and Japan eats far less rice than it used to. Note: FAO food supply.
headline: Rice Buckets

question: Who eats the most tomatoes per person?
stat_label: Tomatoes available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Turkey leads because tomatoes are an everyday food and a huge local crop. Mexico's salsa fame is chiles more than kilos of tomato.
headline: Tomato Towns

question: Who eats the most onions per person?
stat_label: Onions available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Tajik cooking, especially plov, uses onions by the kilo, so a small country leads the world. India's onion dishes add up to much less per person.
headline: Tear Jerkers

question: Which country has the highest suicide rate?
stat_label: Age-standardized suicide rate, both sexes
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator MH_12
fun_fact: Guyana's rate is the world's highest, and pesticide poisoning is the leading method, especially in farming areas. Note: WHO modelled, 2023. Uncertainty is wide where death records are weak.
headline: Global Suicide Rates

question: Which country Googles "anime" the most?
stat_label: Google search interest in the search term "anime"
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, search term, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: Japan ranks last because people there search アニメ, not English 'anime'. Mongolia leads on share of searches, not fan count. Note: each country's own Google searches, scaled to 100.
headline: Anime Searches

question: Which country Googles Lionel Messi the most?
stat_label: Google search interest in Lionel Messi (person topic)
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, topic entity, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: Argentina is not first. Trends scores each country's share of its own searches, so smaller football-mad countries can outrank his home. Note: not search volume or number of fans.
headline: Messi Fans

question: Who gets the most of its energy from renewables?
stat_label: Renewable energy consumption (% of total final energy consumption)
source_name: World Bank (IEA, IRENA, UN Statistics Division, WHO, World Bank: SDG 7.2 tracking)
fun_fact: Uganda beats Norway because firewood and charcoal count as renewable. A high share here often means energy poverty, not green power plants. Note: share of final energy, 2021.
headline: Green Machines

question: Which country spends the biggest share of its economy on the military?
stat_label: Military expenditure (% of GDP)
source_name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database via World Bank
fun_fact: Algeria's share is the army built in the civil war and the rivalry with Morocco, paid for with oil. Poland passed the US share after Russia invaded Ukraine. Note: share of GDP, not dollars. Ukraine, at war, is far higher.
headline: Military Share

question: Where do the most adults use tobacco?
stat_label: Prevalence of current tobacco use, smoked or smokeless (% of adults 15+)
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory via World Bank
fun_fact: France's average beats China's because Chinese women barely smoke, which pulls China's rate down. Note: WHO estimates, adults 15+, any tobacco, not e-cigarettes, 2024.
headline: Smoke Signals

question: Which country is the most forested?
stat_label: Forest area (% of land area)
source_name: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment via World Bank
fun_fact: Japan is more forested than Brazil: steep mountains were hard to farm, Edo-era rules protected the woods, and Japan imports most of its timber. Brazil cleared vast land for cattle and soy. Note: share of land, not hectares.
headline: Into the Woods

question: Where is autism most common?
stat_label: Estimated autism cases per 100 people
source_name: IHME Global Burden of Disease 2023 via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Japan's higher figure mostly reflects more screening and diagnosis, not proof that autism is more common. Note: IHME model built on surveys from relatively few countries.
headline: Autism Rates

question: Which country Googles "Minecraft" the most?
stat_label: Google search interest in the search term "Minecraft"
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, search term, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: Myanmar leads because the word is a large share of its Google searches, not because it has the most players. Note: share of each country's searches, scaled to 100. Language matters.
headline: Minecraft Searches

question: Which country sent its first person to space first?
stat_label: Year the country's first citizen flew to space
source_name: Wikipedia: Timeline of space travel by nationality
fun_fact: Vietnam, Mongolia and Afghanistan flew first as Soviet guests on Soyuz. China waited until it could launch its own astronaut. Note: nationality at launch. Only China flew its own rocket.
headline: Space Race

question: Which country has the most serial killers for its size?
stat_label: Known serial killers relative to population
source_name: Aamodt, M.G. (2016). Serial Killer Statistics. Radford University/FGCU Serial Killer Database
fun_fact: Australia ranks high mainly because English-language cases are documented, not because it has more killers. Note: this database tracks reporting, not true prevalence.
headline: Known Serial Killers

question: Where is reported erect circumference highest?
stat_label: Average reported erect penis circumference, cm
source_name: World Population Review: Penis Size by Country 2026 (data compiled by Little Big Data)
fun_fact: Taiwan, the US and Israel are self-reported, which runs high. Vietnam and Finland were measured in clinics. Note: methods and sample sizes differ, so treat the order as rough.
headline: Reported Circumference

question: Where do the most people view Israel unfavorably?
stat_label: % of adults with an unfavorable view of Israel (Pew Research Center, spring 2026)
source_name: Pew Research Center, Spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey (short read, June 4 2026)
fun_fact: Turkey is the most negative of 36 places Pew surveyed. Views there have been deeply unfavorable for years. Note: spring 2026. Most interviews came after the US-Israel campaign in Iran began on 28 Feb.
headline: Views of Israel

question: Where is the maternal mortality ratio highest?
stat_label: Maternal mortality ratio (deaths per 100,000 live births), 2020
source_name: Wikipedia: List of countries by maternal mortality ratio (WHO Global Health Observatory / UN MMEIG estimates via Our World in Data), 2020 column
fun_fact: The US ranks worse than much poorer countries. Uneven care is one reason, and a pregnancy checkbox on death certificates can mislabel some deaths. Note: UN modelled estimates, 2020. Small countries swing year to year.
headline: Maternal Mortality

question: Which country has the highest homicide rate?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people (UNODC via World Bank, latest year per country, 2021–2023)
source_name: World Bank / UNODC: Intentional homicides (VC.IHR.PSRC.P5)
fun_fact: Costa Rica's rate jumped as cocaine routes and gang fights reached a tourist country. Note: police-recorded homicides. Years differ by country.
headline: Recorded Homicides

question: Which country has the highest homicide rate?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people (UNODC via World Bank, latest year per country, 2022–2023)
source_name: World Bank / UNODC: Intentional homicides (VC.IHR.PSRC.P5)
fun_fact: Jamaica's rate is a long gang-and-gun crisis. Uruguay's rise is newer: cocaine routes reached a country long seen as safe. Note: police-recorded. Years differ by country.
headline: Homicide Figures

question: Where is the female homicide rate highest?
stat_label: Intentional homicide victims, female, per 100,000 women (UNODC via World Bank), 2022
source_name: World Bank / UNODC: Intentional homicides, female (VC.IHR.PSRC.FE.P5)
fun_fact: Latvia's female rate tops Russia's. Across Europe, most women who are killed die at the hands of a partner or relative. Note: police-recorded, 2022. Small countries swing year to year.
headline: Homicide, Women

question: Where do women have the most children?
stat_label: Total fertility rate (births per woman), 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Fertility rate, total (SP.DYN.TFRT.IN)
fun_fact: Saudi Arabia's rate fell as women stayed in school longer. South Korea's collapse tracks costly housing, long hours and very few marriages. India is now below replacement.
headline: Cradle Rockers

question: Where do women have the most children?
stat_label: Total fertility rate (births per woman), 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Fertility rate, total (SP.DYN.TFRT.IN)
fun_fact: Niger stays near the world's top because marriage is early and contraception is still uncommon. Ukraine's rate, already low, fell further during the war.
headline: Full House

question: Where are the most babies born per person?
stat_label: Births per 1,000 people per year (crude birth rate), 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Birth rate, crude (SP.DYN.CBRT.IN)
fun_fact: Israel's birth rate stays high in a rich country because religious Jewish families have many children.
headline: Cradle Count

question: Where do the most teenagers give birth?
stat_label: Births per 1,000 women aged 15–19 (adolescent fertility rate), 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Adolescent fertility rate (SP.ADO.TFRT)
fun_fact: Bulgaria's teen-birth rate is about three times the US rate. Researchers link the high EU rates in Bulgaria and Romania to earlier childbearing in Roma communities. Note: births per 1,000 girls aged 15-19, 2024.
headline: Teen Births

question: Where do the most teenagers give birth?
stat_label: Births per 1,000 women aged 15–19 (adolescent fertility rate), 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Adolescent fertility rate (SP.ADO.TFRT)
fun_fact: Niger's rate is among the world's highest, where marriage is early and contraception is uncommon. Romania is still several times the UK. South Korea is close to zero. Note: births per 1,000 girls aged 15-19, 2024.
headline: Adolescent Births

question: Which country locks up the most people?
stat_label: Prisoners per 100,000 people
source_name: Our World in Data / World Prison Brief: Prison population rate
fun_fact: El Salvador's rate exploded after the 2022 gang crackdown jailed tens of thousands. Japan's stays low, with little violent crime and shorter stays. Note: includes people awaiting trial. Years differ.
headline: Prison Rates

question: Which country locks up the most people?
stat_label: Prisoners per 100,000 people
source_name: Our World in Data / World Prison Brief: Prison population rate
fun_fact: Cuba and Rwanda imprison a larger share than Russia. India's rate is among the world's lowest even though its jails are crowded, because the population is so large. Note: includes pre-trial detention. Years differ.
headline: Behind Bars

question: Where are the roads deadliest?
stat_label: Road traffic deaths per 100,000 people (WHO estimate), 2019
source_name: World Bank / WHO: Mortality caused by road traffic injury (SH.STA.TRAF.P5)
fun_fact: The Dominican Republic has the world's deadliest roads, largely motorcycles and weak enforcement. Japan stays low with strict licensing. Note: WHO modelled estimates, 2019.
headline: Road Deaths

question: Where are the roads deadliest?
stat_label: Road traffic deaths per 100,000 people (WHO estimate), 2019
source_name: World Bank / WHO: Mortality caused by road traffic injury (SH.STA.TRAF.P5)
fun_fact: Rich Saudi Arabia has deadlier roads than India: high speeds and, for years, low seatbelt use. Note: WHO modelled estimates, 2019.
headline: Traffic Deaths

question: Where do women outlive men by the most?
stat_label: Female minus male life expectancy at birth, years, 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Life expectancy at birth, female and male (SP.DYN.LE00.FE.IN / .MA.IN)
fun_fact: Russian women outlive men by the world's biggest gap, mostly because men die early from alcohol and heart disease. Note: female minus male life expectancy, 2024.
headline: Longevity Gap

question: Where is the drug-death rate highest?
stat_label: Deaths from drug use disorders per 100,000 people (IHME Global Burden of Disease), 2021
source_name: Our World in Data / IHME GBD: Death rate from drug use disorders
fun_fact: The US leads because of fentanyl. Mexico's cartel image is trafficking violence, which this measure does not count. Note: IHME estimates, mostly overdoses.
headline: Drug Deaths

question: Which country has the highest adult obesity rate?
stat_label: Adults (18+) with obesity, BMI ≥ 30 (crude estimate), 2024
source_name: Our World in Data / WHO (NCD-RisC): Share of adults who are obese
fun_fact: Tonga's rate followed a switch from fish and root vegetables to imported fatty food. Japan's stays near the bottom of the world.
headline: Belt Notches

question: Who lives the longest?
stat_label: Life expectancy at birth, years, 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN Population Division): Life expectancy at birth (SP.DYN.LE00.IN)
fun_fact: Poor Albania outlives Russia because Russian men die young from alcohol and heart disease. Nigeria's life expectancy is the lowest in the World Bank series.
headline: Built to Last

question: Who drinks the most alcohol per person?
stat_label: Total alcohol per capita (age 15+), litres of pure alcohol, 2020
source_name: World Bank / WHO: Total alcohol consumption per capita (SH.ALC.PCAP.LI)
fun_fact: Latvia out-drinks Russia once home-distilled spirits are counted. Iran's small figure is unrecorded drinking despite a ban. Note: WHO 2020, recorded plus unrecorded, age 15+.
headline: Another Round

question: Where is the infant mortality rate highest?
stat_label: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births, 2024
source_name: World Bank (UN IGME): Mortality rate, infant (SP.DYN.IMRT.IN)
fun_fact: Pakistan's rate is among the world's highest. Cuba, long praised for infant care, is now above the US in the UN estimates. Note: UN IGME modelled estimates, 2024.
headline: Infant Mortality

question: Where do the most people use the internet?
stat_label: Individuals using the internet (% of population), 2024
source_name: World Bank / ITU: Individuals using the Internet (IT.NET.USER.ZS)
fun_fact: Saudi Arabia reports everyone online: a young population and cheap mobile data. Japan is lower mostly because many older people never went online. Note: used the internet in the last 3 months.
headline: Extremely Online

question: Which parliament has the most women?
stat_label: Seats held by women in national parliament (%), 2025
source_name: World Bank / IPU: Proportion of seats held by women in national parliaments (SG.GEN.PARL.ZS)
fun_fact: Cuba's share comes from party lists that place women high. Japan has no binding quota, so parties rarely pick women. Nigeria is near the bottom.
headline: Seats at the Table

question: Which country spends the biggest share of its economy on the military?
stat_label: Military expenditure (% of GDP), 2025
source_name: World Bank / SIPRI: Military expenditure (% of GDP) (MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS)
fun_fact: Ukraine's share is the war itself. Ireland stays near the bottom on a long policy of military neutrality. Note: share of GDP, not dollars.
headline: Defense Budgets

question: Where do the most adults use tobacco?
stat_label: Prevalence of current tobacco use, smoked or smokeless (% of adults 15+), 2024
source_name: World Bank / WHO: Prevalence of current tobacco use (SH.PRV.SMOK)
fun_fact: Lebanon's rate includes heavy shisha use, which this measure counts as tobacco. Germany still uses more than the US, and e-cigarettes are left out. Note: WHO age-standardised estimates, 2024.
headline: Up in Smoke

question: Which country is the most forested?
stat_label: Forest area (% of land area), 2024

question: Where do the most adults use cannabis?
stat_label: Annual prevalence of cannabis use (% of people aged 15-64)
source_name: UNODC World Drug Report 2026, Statistical Annex, Table 1.2
fun_fact: Canada leads because past-year use in this UNODC series rose from 14.8% in 2017 to 32.4% in 2023, after legalization. The Netherlands still sits below France: Dutch possession remains a crime, and coffeeshops only tolerate sales of up to 5 grams. Note: latest survey per country, 2023 or 2024. Household surveys. Age bands differ. Canada is ages 15+, France is 18-64, and the US figure is UNODC's adjustment to 15-64.
